artiest/piet-veerman.text:
Piet Veerman is a Dutch pop musician, born in 1943 in the fishing village of Volendam. His father played many instruments and taught him music; his mother was a painter. At twelve he received his first guitar. With his cousin Jaap Schilder he performed as the Everly Kosters, a reference to The Everly Brothers. Then came The Mystic Four, which became The Blue Cats and eventually The Cats.

From 1964 to 1985 Veerman was guitarist and singer of The Cats, and from the single Times Were When in 1968 he sang almost all of the singles. Until 1974 it was the most popular Dutch band, also in Belgium, Germany, Indonesia and Suriname. The band split up in 1974 and reunited in 1975, when Veerman made an album and a single, both called Rollin' On A River, which reached number nine in the Top 40. In 1980 the group stopped again. After the final break-up he started a solo career in 1987 with Sailin' Home, an adaptation of Zora je by Neda Ukraden. It reached number one in the Netherlands and Belgium and in the Netherlands was the best-selling single of the year. He received more than thirty gold records.

Later he tried reggae and soul, with covers of Willy DeVille, and recorded songs partly in Spanish, with influences of Latin pop and Tex-Mex. He also worked with other Volendammers, such as Anny Schilder, Jan Smit and George Baker. Veerman gave the Volendam sound a recognisable face: soft singing, melodic guitars and simple, warm songs.
artiest/piet-veerman.listen: Listen to Sailin' Home and notice the warm, calm singing voice and the simple structure of the chorus. Try to hear how little the song needs to stay in your head for good.

artiest/pim-jacobs.text:
Pim Jacobs (1934 to 1996) was a Dutch jazz pianist, composer and television presenter, born in Hilversum. He began playing the piano at the age of six. His brother Ruud, born in 1938, became a jazz bassist. In 1954 they formed a trio with the drummer Wessel Ilcken. Later the guitarist Wim Overgaauw and Ilcken's wife, the singer Rita Reys, joined them. In 1956 they recorded with Herbie Mann. After Ilcken's death in 1957 Pim Jacobs played with Reys as a duo or with Overgaauw as a trio. In 1960 Jacobs and Reys married.

The Pim Jacobs Trio became famous and performed at festivals in many European cities and in New Orleans. The programme consisted of arrangements of vocal standards and bebop numbers. The trio also accompanied singers such as Tony Bennett and Ella Fitzgerald. Jacobs worked with Louis van Dijk and recorded with his trio with Bob Cooper. He also wrote film music. From 1964 he worked in radio and television, and presented the music programme Music for All on television. In the 1970s and 1980s he gave concerts in schools. For charity he played with Louis van Dijk and Pieter van Vollenhoven under the name Gevleugelde vrienden (Winged Friends).

Jacobs brought modern jazz to a wide Dutch audience, with accessible arrangements and a friendly presentation. The Pim Jacobs Theater in Maarssen is named after him. His cousin Bobby Jacobs became a member of the rock band Focus.
artiest/pim-jacobs.listen: Listen to a recording of the Pim Jacobs Trio with Rita Reys and notice how the singer and the piano answer each other. Try to hear how light and swinging the accompaniment remains.

artiest/pinar-toprak.text: Pinar Toprak (born in 1980 in Istanbul) studied at Berklee in Boston and then settled in Los Angeles. She wrote music for films, television and games. For the series Krypton (2018) she created a large orchestral sound around Superman's family. For Fortnite: Save the World she worked on one of the biggest games in the world. With Captain Marvel (2019) she became the first woman to score a film of the Marvel Cinematic Universe as sole composer. Her theme for the heroine combines a powerful brass fanfare with a warm, human side. Later she also wrote the music for the game Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora (2023).
artiest/pinar-toprak.listen: Listen to the heroic brass line with electronic pulses beneath it, and to how the theme grows bigger as the orchestra plays more fully.

artiest/pine-top-smith.text:
Clarence Pinetop Smith was born in Alabama in 1904, the son of Sam and Molly Smith. He got his nickname as a child because he liked climbing trees. As a teenager he moved with his family to Birmingham, and in 1920 he went to Pittsburgh. There he worked as an entertainer and toured the T.O.B.A. vaudeville circuit as a singer, comedian and pianist. For a time he accompanied Ma Rainey and Butterbeans and Susie.

In 1928 Smith moved with his wife and little son to Chicago to record. Cow Cow Davenport had recommended him to Vocalion Records. For a time he lived in the same boarding house as Albert Ammons and Meade Lux Lewis, two other pianists in the same style. On 29 December 1928 he recorded Pine Top's Boogie Woogie. It became a hit and gave the style its name. It was also the first record with the words boogie woogie in the title. During the recording Smith talks about the piece and tells you how to dance to it. He said he had made it up at a house party in St. Louis to pay the rent.

The pianist plays a rhythmically rolling pattern in the left hand, with striking breaks that come from ragtime and point forward to rock 'n' roll. Smith died in 1929, at the age of twenty-four. His record is thus one of the most important examples of boogie-woogie, and the style lived on in the pianists who came after him, such as Ammons, Lewis and Pete Johnson.
artiest/pine-top-smith.listen: Listen to Pine Top's Boogie Woogie. Notice Smith's voice telling you, between the playing, how to dance, and the breaks in which the rhythm briefly drops out.

artiest/pink.text:
Pink, the stage name of Alecia Moore, is an American singer from Doylestown, Pennsylvania. She began in the 1990s in a girl group, but around 2000 went her own way as a solo artist. Her debut album Can't Take Me Home appeared in 2000 and brought her a first string of hits. With Missundaztood, from 2001, she deliberately chose a more individual and more rock-oriented sound.

Pink's music moves between pop, rock and R&B. Her voice is raw and powerful, and her songs combine a razor-sharp tone with catchy choruses. Later came albums such as I'm Not Dead and The Truth About Love, and songs such as So What became known worldwide. She is also known for her spectacular live shows, in which acrobatics play a large part.

In the course Pink appears in a row of big names for whom the hit factory of Swedish and American songwriters and producers worked. That shows how a pop star of this size operates: the singer is the face and the voice, while a team of writers and producers helps shape the songs.
artiest/pink.listen: Listen to So What and notice the combination of a tight pop rhythm and guitars that sound almost like rock. Can you hear how the voice switches between mocking and exuberant?

artiest/pink-floyd.text:
Pink Floyd was formed in London in 1965 by Syd Barrett, Roger Waters, Nick Mason and Richard Wright. The name came from two blues musicians whose records Barrett owned: Pink Anderson and Floyd Council. The group began as a psychedelic band in the London underground and then became one of the most important names in progressive rock, in which the album became a continuous whole.

In clubs such as the UFO Club, Pink Floyd played under light shows projected onto the band. The debut album The Piper at the Gates of Dawn (1967) opens with Barrett's Astronomy Domine. At the end of 1967 or the beginning of 1968 the guitarist David Gilmour joined, and in 1968 Barrett, whose mental health was deteriorating, left. Waters became the main lyricist. The Dark Side of the Moon (1973) is one continuous work about time, money, pressure and madness, with songs that flow into one another. The prism on the sleeve came from the design studio Hipgnosis. The album stayed in the American album chart for more than fourteen years. Wish You Were Here (1975), Animals (1977) and The Wall (1979), with the hit Another Brick in the Wall (Part 2), followed.

In 1985 Waters left; Gilmour and Mason carried on under the name Pink Floyd. Barrett died in 2006, Wright in 2008. In 2005 Gilmour, Waters, Mason and Wright stood on stage together one last time, at Live 8 in London. The band showed that a rock album could be a composition, with studio sounds and effects as part of the music.
artiest/pink-floyd.listen: Money is largely in 7/4 time. The rhythm begins with a tape loop of coins, a cash register and tearing paper. Count along: after seven beats the loop starts again. At the guitar solo the band switches to an ordinary four.

artiest/pinto-colvig.text:
Pinto Colvig (1892 to 1967) was an American actor, cartoonist, animator and circus and vaudeville performer. He was born Vance DeBar Colvig in Jacksonville, Oregon. He got his nickname at the age of seven, because of his freckles and his pranks. He played clarinet in the band of the Al G. Barnes Circus and drew for newspapers. His act was playing the clarinet while pulling faces, with deliberately wrong notes.

In the 1920s he moved to Hollywood, where he worked as an animator, writer and comedian in silent films and in sound cartoons. In 1930 he signed a contract with Walt Disney Productions, at first as a writer. He also made sound effects, such as Pluto's barking. From 1931 he voiced Goofy, who was then still called Dippy Dawg. He also voiced Practical Pig in Three Little Pigs and both Grumpy and Sleepy in Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs. After a quarrel with Disney he worked elsewhere between 1939 and 1943. For Fleischer he voiced Bluto in the Popeye cartoons and Gabby in Gulliver's Travels. He was also a Munchkin in The Wizard of Oz of 1939.

In 1946 he became Bozo the Clown for Capitol Records, a role he played for ten years, on television too. In that period he recorded the song Filbert the Frog, in which he used the glottal stop as a musical instrument. His last appearance, in 1967, was as Goofy for the Telephone Pavilion at Expo 67. In 1993 he was posthumously named a Disney Legend. Colvig shows how the voice itself can be an instrument in popular culture.
artiest/pinto-colvig.listen: Listen to Goofy in an old Disney cartoon and notice how the voice is used almost musically. Try to hear how laughter and sound effects merge in his voice.

artiest/pixies.text:
Pixies is an American alternative rock band from Boston, formed in 1986. Singer and guitarist Black Francis and guitarist Joey Santiago met at university in Amherst. Francis placed an advertisement for a bassist who liked both Peter, Paul and Mary and the punk band Hüsker Dü. Kim Deal was the only one who answered, and she came to the audition without a bass because she had never played one. Drummer David Lovering completed the group. Santiago picked the name at random from a dictionary.

After the mini-album Come On Pilgrim (1987) came Surfer Rosa (1988), recorded in two weeks with Steve Albini. It contains Where Is My Mind?. Doolittle (1989), Bossanova (1990) and Trompe le Monde (1991) followed. The Pixies sound revolves around sudden shifts between soft and loud: quiet verses with a tight bass line and then an explosion of guitars and screaming. There are influences of punk and surf rock in it. Francis wrote strange, surreal lyrics about aliens, Biblical violence and other unusual subjects.

In America success remained modest, but in England and the rest of Europe, the Netherlands included, the band attracted a great deal of attention. In 1993 the group broke up. Only afterwards did the influence grow: Nirvana, Radiohead, The Smashing Pumpkins and Weezer learned from Pixies. Kurt Cobain admitted that Smells Like Teen Spirit was an attempt to imitate Pixies. In 2004 the band got back together.
artiest/pixies.listen: Listen to Where Is My Mind? and notice Kim Deal's high, floating voice in the background. Hear, too, how the guitar plays a simple, plaintive melody above the solid rhythm guitar.

artiest/pixinguinha.text: Pixinguinha, born Alfredo da Rocha Viana Filho in Rio de Janeiro, was a flautist, saxophonist, arranger and composer of choro. In the early 1920s he played for months in Paris with his group Os Oito Batutas. His Carinhoso, which appeared around 1930, became one of the best-loved Brazilian melodies. Later he recorded duets on saxophone with the flautist Benedito Lacerda, in which two melodies constantly play around each other.
artiest/pixinguinha.listen: Listen to Um a Zero: Lacerda's flute plays the melody, and Pixinguinha's saxophone winds a second line around it.

artiest/pixinguinha-en-benedito-lacerda.text:
Pixinguinha was the nickname of Alfredo da Rocha Viana Filho, a Brazilian composer, arranger, flautist and saxophonist, born in 1897 in Rio de Janeiro. His father was a flautist and owned a large collection of choro scores. He regularly held music evenings at home. In 1912 Pixinguinha was already playing in cabarets and revues in the Lapa district. Later he became flautist in the house orchestra of the Cine Rio Branco cinema, where live music accompanied silent films. In 1914 he formed the band Caxangá with his friends João Pernambuco and Donga.

In 1919 he founded Os Oito Batutas with his brother and other musicians. The line-up was at first traditional, with flute, guitars, cavaquinho, banjo cavaquinho and hand percussion. The group played in the lobby of the Cine Palais cinema, and its music soon became more popular than the films themselves. It played folk music from the north-east of Brazil, sambas, maxixes, waltzes, polkas and Brazilian tangos. Black and white musicians played together, and this happened in places where Black performers had not previously been admitted. That led to a debate about race and about the influence of Europe and the United States on Brazilian music.

Pixinguinha developed the choro, a style that combines Afro-Brazilian rhythms with European influences. He joined the music of nineteenth-century composers with modern, jazz-influenced harmonies and refined arrangements. He was one of the first Brazilian musicians to embrace radio and the studio. His best-known compositions are Carinhoso, Glória, Lamento and Um a Zero. The course mentions Um a Zero from 1946 together with Benedito Lacerda, about whom the local source file says nothing, so this text follows Pixinguinha alone.
artiest/pixinguinha-en-benedito-lacerda.listen: Listen to Um a Zero. Notice how the flute and the saxophone play around each other like two voices, above a light, danceable rhythm.

artiest/pjotr-iljitsj-tsjaikovski.text: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky studied at the new conservatory in St Petersburg and became a teacher in Moscow. Unlike the Group of Five, he mastered Western forms thoroughly, but his melodies and colours remained Russian. With Swan Lake, The Sleeping Beauty and The Nutcracker he made great symphonic art of ballet music. His Sixth Symphony ends with a slowly dying lament; nine days after the premiere in 1893 he died.
artiest/pjotr-iljitsj-tsjaikovski.listen: Listen to the scene from Swan Lake and hear how the oboe sings the swan theme above trembling strings and harp.

artiest/planxty.text:
Planxty was an Irish folk band that began in January 1972. The first line-up consisted of Christy Moore on vocals, acoustic guitar and bodhrán, Andy Irvine on vocals, mandolin, mandola, bouzouki, hurdy-gurdy and harmonica, Dónal Lunny on bouzouki, guitars, bodhrán and keyboards, and Liam O'Flynn on uilleann pipes and tin whistle. Moore and Lunny had been friends since their schooldays in Newbridge, and Lunny had taught Moore to play guitar and bodhrán. The four came together in the summer of 1971 at the recording of Moore's second solo album, Prosperous.

The band recorded their first single, Three Drunken Maidens, on 18 January 1972. The first big performance was as the support act for Donovan in Galway. The record brought the first successes, and in 1973 the debut album Planxty appeared. The Well Below the Valley (1973) and Cold Blow and the Rainy Night (1974) followed. The third album and the later records brought in other musicians, such as Johnny Moynihan, Paul Brady, Matt Molloy and Bill Whelan. The band stopped for the first time in 1975, played again from 1979 to 1983, and got together one more time in the original line-up in 2003. The last performance was on 31 January 2005.

Planxty changed Irish folk music and made it popular. They brought old ballads and dance tunes with a clear interplay of their own between stringed instruments and the uilleann pipes. As a result traditional music sounded for the first time like a real band. Planxty Irwin from 1973, the piece in the course, is in such Irish music an instrumental example of a planxty, a kind of tribute to a patron.
artiest/planxty.listen: Listen to Planxty Irwin. Try to tell the different stringed instruments and the uilleann pipes apart and notice how they play the melody together.

artiest/plas-johnson.text:
Plas Johnson (1931 to 2026) was an American tenor saxophonist in soul-jazz and hard bop, born in Donaldsonville, Louisiana. He first sang in the family group until his father, also a saxophonist, bought him a soprano saxophone. He was largely self-taught and soon took up alto and later tenor saxophone. In the late 1940s he recorded in New Orleans with his brother, the pianist Ray, as the Johnson Brothers. In 1951 he toured for the first time with R&B singer Charles Brown. After his army service during the Korean War he moved in 1954 with his brother to Los Angeles.

There he became a session musician, working for B.B. King and Johnny Otis, among others. In the mid-1950s he came to Capitol Records through Johnny Otis. For almost twenty years he was a leading studio musician, averaging two sessions a day. He played on records by Peggy Lee, Nat King Cole and Frank Sinatra, on rock 'n' roll singles by Duane Eddy and Ricky Nelson, on many recordings by the Beach Boys and for groups that existed only in the studio, such as B. Bumble and the Stingers and The Marketts. He appears in the 2008 documentary The Wrecking Crew.

His best-known achievement is the tenor saxophone solo in The Pink Panther Theme by Henry Mancini, recorded in 1963. Unlike many studio musicians, he became known by name. In this way he is an example of how a session musician shapes the sound of an era, without always being on the sleeve.
artiest/plas-johnson.listen: Listen to The Pink Panther Theme by Henry Mancini and notice the low, prowling tenor saxophone. Try to hear how the soloist carries the melody with a free, loose, bluesy tone.

artiest/poison.text:
Poison was an American rock band from Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania. The group began in 1983 under the name Paris and moved to Los Angeles that same year. In the clubs of the Sunset Strip it built an audience with an exuberant show and a deliberate image. The best-known line-up consisted of singer Bret Michaels, drummer Rikki Rockett, bassist Bobby Dall and guitarist C.C. DeVille, who in 1985 replaced the first guitarist Matt Smith.

The debut album Look What the Cat Dragged In appeared in 1986 and was the breakthrough. Open Up and Say... Ahh! followed in 1988 and Flesh & Blood in 1990. With Every Rose Has Its Thorn the band reached number one on the American Hot 100. Other singles were Talk Dirty to Me, Nothin' But a Good Time and Unskinny Bop. In the 1990s the band lost ground when grunge arrived, but it kept performing and came back in 1999 in the original line-up.

Poison played glam metal: hard rock with souped-up guitars, sing-along choruses, plenty of hairspray and make-up. The genre was about image and fun, and Poison counted as one of its examples. In the course the band appears beside Mötley Crüe as a textbook case of 1980s glam metal.
artiest/poison.listen: Listen to Talk Dirty to Me and notice the sharp, melodic guitar solo and the cheerful sing-along chorus. What makes this different from the heavier metal of the time?

artiest/poly-styrene.text:
Poly Styrene was the stage name of Marianne Joan Elliott-Said (1957 to 2011), the singer of the punk band X-Ray Spex. She was born in Bromley and grew up in Brixton, London, the daughter of a Scottish-Irish mother and a Somali father. As a teenager she was a hippie, and at fifteen she ran away from home to hitchhike from festival to festival. In 1976 she released the reggae single Silly Billy under her own name, Mari Elliott.

After a Sex Pistols gig in an empty hall on Hastings Pier she placed an advertisement in the music papers for young punks who wanted to join forces. This is how X-Ray Spex came into being, and she took her stage name from the Yellow Pages. The band's debut was a single in 1977, and the album Germfree Adolescents followed. Billboard called her the prototype of modern feminist punk. She wore braces on her teeth, resisted the image of woman as sex object in the 1970s and wore striking clothes. Her voice was described as a bold, wailing cry.

After the band broke up in 1979 she made the solo album Translucence in 1980, calmer and jazzier. She released Flower Aeroplane in 2004 and Generation Indigo in 2011, shortly before her death from breast cancer in April 2011. In 1983 she joined the Hare Krishna movement. In 2023 Rolling Stone placed her at number 195 of the two hundred greatest singers of all time.
artiest/poly-styrene.listen: Listen to Oh Bondage Up Yours! by X-Ray Spex and notice Poly Styrene's shrill, angular voice above the powerful guitars. Try to hear where she almost shouts her lines instead of singing them.

artiest/ponthon-tielman.text:
Ponthon Tielman (died in 2000) was the bassist of the Tielman Brothers, the first Dutch-Indonesian band to have international success. He grew up in Indonesia with his brothers Andy, who sang and played guitar, Reggy on guitar and Loulou on drums. The family came from Kupang in eastern Indonesia. In Indonesia the brothers first played under the names Timor Brothers and The Four T's. In 1956 they moved to the Netherlands, first to Breda and later to The Hague.

The band played a kind of rock 'n' roll that later became known as Indorock: a mixture of Indonesian and Western music with roots in kroncong. Their performances were spectacular. The brothers threw their guitars to each other and Ponthon played the bass with his teeth. In 1958 the band stood out as a stand-in act at the World's Fair in Brussels. A quarter of an hour of filling in became a show that drove the audience wild, after which they were allowed to play in German clubs, including on the Reeperbahn in Hamburg. After the World's Fair their first single, Rock Little Baby of Mine, came out on the Belgian label Fernap Records. That is the first Dutch rock 'n' roll record. In 1959 the band signed with Imperial Records.

Later the band moved to Australia, possibly because of racism and because the brothers felt they received too little recognition. In 1983 Andy Tielman disbanded the group. Ponthon died in 2000.
artiest/ponthon-tielman.listen: Listen to Rock Little Baby of Mine and notice the raw, fast rock 'n' roll sound. Try to hear how the bass carries the rhythm.

artiest/pools-nationaal-radio-symfonieor.text:
The Polish National Radio Symphony Orchestra, in Polish Narodowa Orkiestra Symfoniczna Polskiego Radia, NOSPR for short, is one of the most important radio orchestras and musical institutions in Poland. The orchestra was founded in 1935 in Warsaw under the direction of Grzegorz Fitelberg, until the Second World War broke out. In March 1945 it was revived in Katowice by Witold Rowicki. In 1947 Fitelberg returned from abroad and resumed the artistic direction. Since 2006 it has been a National Cultural Institution. In 2019 the orchestra joined the European Concert Hall Organisation.

The long list of conductors and soloists who worked with the orchestra includes Leonard Bernstein, Krzysztof Penderecki, Witold Lutosławski, Kurt Masur, Charles Mackerras, Martha Argerich, Artur Rubinstein and Mstislav Rostropovich. Among the music directors were Jan Krenz and Bohdan Wodiczko. Since the 2023 to 2024 season Marin Alsop has been artistic director and principal conductor.

The orchestra's albums show a wide repertoire. It played symphonies, violin concertos and piano concertos from the late Romantic period, symphonic poems, overtures and also Polish works, such as the Symphony of Sorrowful Songs by Henryk Górecki, which appears in the album list. The orchestra belongs to the Polish post-war musical culture that attracted international attention, and remains open to contemporary collaboration, including with the singer Ledisi.
artiest/pools-nationaal-radio-symfonieor.listen: Listen to a recording by the orchestra of a Polish symphony and notice the long, slow string sounds. Try to hear how the orchestra holds that stillness without the tension falling away.

artiest/pop-smoke.text:
Pop Smoke was the stage name of Bashar Barakah Jackson, an American rapper and singer. He was born in 1999 in Brooklyn, New York, the son of a Jamaican mother and a Panamanian father. As a child he played African drums and sang in his neighbourhood church. His name is a combination of Poppa, as his Panamanian grandmother called him, and Smocco Guwop, a nickname from childhood friends. In 2018 he tried rapping for the first time, in a recording studio in Brooklyn.

In 2019 he broke through with the singles Welcome to the Party and Dior. That year he signed a contract with Victor Victor Worldwide and Republic Records, and in July his first mixtape, Meet the Woo, appeared. His second, Meet the Woo 2, came out on 7 February 2020 and immediately entered the American top ten of the album chart. Twelve days later he was murdered during a robbery at his home in Los Angeles. He was twenty years old.

Again and again Pop Smoke collaborated with British drill artists and producers, who made a barer and more aggressive sound than the American drill of Chicago. In this way he brought that style back under the name Brooklyn drill. His deep, raw voice suits those hard beats. His first studio album, Shoot for the Stars, Aim for the Moon (2020), came out after his death, with 50 Cent as executive producer. It topped the Billboard 200. In 2021 Faith followed. He shows how a sound from Chicago and London took on a new face in New York.
artiest/pop-smoke.listen: Listen to Dior. Notice the low, raw voice, the bare, hard beat and how few instruments are needed to make such a menacing sound.

artiest/pop-will-eat-itself.text:
Pop Will Eat Itself, PWEI for short, is an English alternative rock band, formed in 1986 in Stourbridge in the West Midlands, with members from Birmingham, Coventry and the Black Country. The name comes from a piece by David Quantick in the magazine NME. An earlier version of the group was called From Eden and had Clint Mansell as a member. Graham Crabb, Adam Mole, Mansell and Richard March formed the core. Their first single, Poppies Say Grrr!, was sold in a brown paper bag in 1986 and was Single of the Week in NME.

At first they were counted as part of grebo, but samples, hip hop and industrial rock soon found their way into their music. They listened to Run-DMC, Public Enemy and the Beastie Boys, and to sample records by The KLF and Bomb the Bass. Three albums appeared on RCA, including This Is the Day...This Is the Hour...This Is This! and Cure for Sanity, recorded with producer Flood. Hits were Can U Dig It? and Wise Up! Sucker. Their biggest single was Get the Girl! Kill the Baddies! in 1993, a top ten hit in the United Kingdom. In 1992 The Looks or the Lifestyle? appeared with drummer John Townshend.

The group became more political with Ich Bin Ein Auslander, together with Fun-Da-Mental and with anti-Nazi lyrics. In 1996 it broke up. Mansell later became a film composer, for Requiem for a Dream and Black Swan, among others. In this way PWEI shows how punk attitude, hip hop and samplers came together in one sound in the 1980s and 1990s.
artiest/pop-will-eat-itself.listen: Listen to Can U Dig It? and notice how samples and a tight beat carry the song rather than guitars alone. Try to hear which sounds seem borrowed from other music or films.

artiest/porter-wagoner.text:
Porter Wagoner (1927 to 2007) was an American country singer, known for his flamboyant Nudie suits and his blond pompadour. He was born in West Plains, Missouri, the youngest of five children of a farmer. He worked as a butcher's assistant and performed with his first band, the Blue Ridge Boys, on local radio. In 1951 he got a job at radio station KWTO in Springfield, which led to a contract with RCA Victor. In 1955 he became a regular guest on the TV show Ozark Jubilee, and in 1957 he moved to Nashville to become a member of the Grand Ole Opry. There he was called Mr. Grand Ole Opry.

Wagoner had eighty-one records in the charts. His first number one was A Satisfied Mind in 1955, followed by Misery Loves Company in 1962 and, among others, Green, Green Grass of Home, The Cold Hard Facts of Life and The Carroll County Accident. From 1960 to 1981 his TV programme The Porter Wagoner Show ran, with some 686 episodes. In 1967 he introduced the singer Dolly Parton on it. Together they made hits such as The Last Thing on My Mind and Daddy Was An Old Time Preacher Man, until Parton chose her own path. Her song I Will Always Love You, written about that break, topped the country chart in 1974.

Wagoner brought James Brown to the Grand Ole Opry, produced an R&B album for Joe Simon and appeared in Clint Eastwood's Honkytonk Man. In 2002 he was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame.
artiest/porter-wagoner.listen: Listen to Misery Loves Company or a duet with Dolly Parton and notice the storytelling vocals over a simple country accompaniment. Try to hear how the steel guitar follows the singing.

artiest/portishead.text:
Portishead is an English band from the Bristol area. Geoff Barrow and the singer Beth Gibbons met in 1991 during a coffee break at a course for the unemployed. They named the band after Portishead, the town, dull in their eyes, where Barrow came from, about thirteen kilometres west of Bristol. Barrow borrowed records from a local DJ with a large collection of soundtracks and used fragments from them as hip hop loops. During the recording they met the guitarist Adrian Utley, who became an official member shortly after the first album.

The debut album Dummy appeared in 1994, with the singles Numb, Sour Times and Glory Box. It combines the beats and samples of hip hop with an atmosphere reminiscent of old spy films, and with Gibbons's fragile, yearning voice. A music magazine called it musique noire for a film yet to be made. Dummy won the Mercury Prize in 1995 and became a milestone of trip hop, although the band itself did not like that label.

The second album Portishead (1997) sounded grainier and harder, with more live-played instruments and fewer samples. After that it stayed quiet for a long time, until Third in 2008. With Massive Attack and Tricky, Portishead defined the dark, slow sound of Bristol in the 1990s, in which hip hop, soul and film music came together.
artiest/portishead.listen: Listen to Glory Box and notice the slow, constantly repeated sample with strings on which the song rests. Hear how Beth Gibbons's voice floats above it, and how a distorted guitar appears halfway through.

artiest/primal-scream.text:
Primal Scream is a Scottish rock band that began in Glasgow in 1982 around the singer Bobby Gillespie and the guitarist Jim Beattie. Both were school friends and at first made rudimentary sound tapes: Gillespie banged two bin lids together, Beattie played fuzz guitar. Then they played covers of songs by The Velvet Underground and The Byrds and wrote songs of their own, based on bass lines by Jah Wobble and Peter Hook. The name comes from the title track of The Fall's debut album. Primal Scream played live for the first time in 1982.

The career only really got going when Gillespie stopped being the drummer of The Jesus and Mary Chain, where he had for a time switched between two bands. In the mid-1980s the group belonged to the indie pop scene, and Velocity Girl from 1986 is an example from that period. It then moved on to a psychedelic and garage rock sound, with records such as Sonic Flower Groove (1987) and Primal Scream (1989). With Screamadelica in 1991 it added dance music and broke through to the general public.

On later albums the band kept searching. Give Out but Don't Give Up (1994), Vanishing Point (1997) and XTRMNTR (2000) show blues, trip hop and industrial rock. The most recent album, Come Ahead, appeared on 8 November 2024. For pop history Primal Scream is important because it showed that a guitar band from the indie corner could embrace the dance floor and the long party of acid house, without losing its rock side.
artiest/primal-scream.listen: Listen to Velocity Girl. Notice how short the song is and how the guitars sound bright and light, rather than heavy or danceable.

artiest/prime-time.text:
Prime Time was an American free-funk band, founded in 1975 by Ornette Coleman. The music followed his theory of harmolodics, in which melody, harmony and rhythm have no fixed hierarchy. The first members included the guitarists Bern Nix and Charles Ellerbee, the bassist Jamaaladeen Tacuma and the drummers Denardo Coleman and Ronald Shannon Jackson. Later the bassist Albert MacDowell and the drummer Sabir Kamal, among others, joined.

Coleman's first album with Prime Time was Dancing in Your Head. The album Virgin Beauty from 1988, with guest appearances by Jerry Garcia of the Grateful Dead, was their most successful. It reached number two in the Billboard jazz album chart and in its first year sold more than any previous record by Coleman. In 1993 Prime Time played as the opening act for the Grateful Dead at the Oakland Coliseum. In 2017, two years after Ornette's death, his son Denardo brought the group together again for a concert at Alice Tully Hall, as a tribute to Ornette and to Bern Nix, who had died earlier that year.

With Prime Time, Coleman brought free jazz to electric instruments and funk rhythms. The group had two guitarists and two drummers, who played in and out of each other. In this way he linked up with electric jazz and the rock world, and the group became a bridge between the avant-garde and a wider audience.
artiest/prime-time.listen: Listen to Dancing in Your Head and try to keep the two guitars and the rhythm section apart. Notice how they play at the same time without anyone seeming to be in charge.

artiest/prince.text:
Prince Rogers Nelson was born on 7 June 1958 in Minneapolis, the son of a jazz singer and a pianist and songwriter. His father performed as Prince Rogers, and the son was named after that stage name. At only eighteen he signed a contract with Warner Bros., and two years later his first album, For You (1978), appeared.

Critics were enthusiastic about Dirty Mind (1980), Controversy (1981) and 1999 (1982). In 1984 he had the number 1 in America at the cinema, in the album chart and in the singles chart at the same time, with the film Purple Rain, the soundtrack and When Doves Cry. He recorded that album with his backing band The Revolution. Kiss also became a number 1. After The Revolution came the double album Sign o' the Times (1987), which is often regarded as his best work. In 1993, in the middle of a conflict with Warner Bros., he changed his name to an unpronounceable symbol. Only in 2000 did he carry on again as Prince.

Prince was singer, guitarist, keyboard player, bassist, dancer, producer and filmmaker all at once. He mixed funk, rock, pop and soul and was one of the founders of the Minneapolis sound, a tight, electronic kind of funk with synthesizers and drum machines. He worked tirelessly: in his lifetime he released 39 albums and he left a great deal of unreleased material. On 21 April 2016 he died, aged 57, at Paisley Park, his home and studio near Minneapolis, of an overdose of counterfeit painkillers.
artiest/prince.listen: Listen to When Doves Cry (1984). Notice what is missing: the song has no bass part. Hear how the drum machine, the synthesizer and Prince's voices together fill the space.

artiest/prince-buster.text:
Prince Buster, born Cecil Bustamente Campbell, was a Jamaican singer, writer and producer. He was born in 1938 on Orange Street in Kingston. As a young man he moved in the world of the sound systems, the mobile discos that played American rhythm and blues. He worked for Coxsone Dodd and then started his own sound system, Voice of the People. Because he could not get records from the United States, he decided to record music himself.

In 1961 he released his first single and produced Oh Carolina by the Folkes Brothers, with drummers from the Count Ossie Group. Through the English label Blue Beat his music reached the British public. In the 1960s he recorded an enormous amount. Well-known ska songs from that time are Madness, Wash Wash, One Step Beyond and Al Capone. With Al Capone he reached the British top twenty in 1967. When the music became slower and more soulful, he also wrote rocksteady, for example on the album Judge Dread Rock Steady.

His records formed the basis of later ska and reggae. In England his work found a second life with the two-tone groups of the late 1970s. The band Madness took its name from his song Madness and also played One Step Beyond, the title of his song from 1964. In this way a line runs from Kingston in the 1960s to the youth culture of England.
artiest/prince-buster.listen: Listen to Madness or Al Capone and notice the rhythm: the guitar strikes the offbeat, the bass walks along and the horns fill in. This is what early ska sounds like.

artiest/prince-en-the-revolution.text:
The Revolution was an American funk rock band from Minneapolis, formed in 1979 by Prince, at first as his live band and later also as a studio band. The group began as a multiracial ensemble of men and women, following the example of Sly Stone. The first line-up consisted of Prince, Dez Dickerson on guitar, Andre Cymone on bass, Bobby Z. on drums and the keyboard players Gayle Chapman and Matt Fink. In 1979 Prince recorded material in Colorado with the group as a side project, The Rebels.

The band was first heard on the studio record 1999 from 1982. It became world famous with Purple Rain in 1984, the album that topped the Billboard 200. Around the World in a Day followed in 1985 and also reached number one. The band had six top ten singles in the Billboard Hot 100, including three number ones: Let's Go Crazy, When Doves Cry and Kiss. The sound combined rock, funk, R&B, new wave, synth-pop and psychedelia. Together with Prince's other projects it created the Minneapolis sound.

After the tour in support of Parade, the soundtrack of Under the Cherry Moon, the group broke up in 1986. After Prince's death in 2016 it announced reunion concerts. The Revolution won three Grammys. It showed how a band of different backgrounds could make rock and funk sound together.
artiest/prince-en-the-revolution.listen: Listen to When Doves Cry and notice what is missing: there is no bass guitar. Try to hear how the drum machine and the synthesizers carry the song all the same.

artiest/prince-nico-mbarga.text:
Prince Nico Mbarga (1950 to 1997) was a Cameroonian-Nigerian highlife musician, born in Abakaliki in Nigeria, the son of a Nigerian mother and a Cameroonian father. He grew up in Ikom and as a boy heard his first highlife on a second-hand radio: Taxi Driver by Bobby Benson. His father came from a family of xylophone players and taught him the instrument. Mbarga built a xylophone himself from dried plantain skins and bark, because he wanted a sound more like Western instruments.

During the Nigerian civil war he fled in 1967 to Mamfe in Cameroon. There he worked as a band boy for a Congolese group and got to know Congolese rumba. He became self-taught on conga, bass and electric guitar in Congolese finger-picking style. Back in Nigeria he first had a regional hit with his band Rocafil Jazz with I No Go Marry My Papa. Then in 1976 came Sweet Mother, sung in Pidgin, which became one of the best-selling records in Nigerian music history. With Rogers All Stars the band recorded nine albums between 1975 and 1981.

Mbarga created a mixture of Nigerian and Congolese guitar styles of his own, with soft vocals and light acoustic melodies. In 1982 he performed in England, known for his glam-rock-style clothes. Sweet Mother is sometimes called the anthem of Africa. He was killed in a motorcycle accident in Calabar in 1997.
artiest/prince-nico-mbarga.listen: Listen to Sweet Mother and notice the light, rhythmic guitars weaving over one another. Try to hear how the singing enters into a conversation with the band.

artiest/prince-nico-mbarga-en-rocafil-ja.text:
Prince Nico Mbarga was a highlife musician with two passports, one Cameroonian and one Nigerian. He was born in 1950 in Abakaliki in Nigeria, the son of a Nigerian mother and a Cameroonian father. He grew up in Ikom, where his father was a sawyer. His passion for highlife began when his father brought home a second-hand Philips radio. The sounds of Taxi Driver by Bobby Benson struck him. His father came from a long line of xylophone players and taught him the instrument. Mbarga, however, wanted a sound closer to the Western instruments of highlife, and built a xylophone himself from dried banana skins and bark.

After his father's death life became hard. He sang in bars, often without being paid. During the Nigerian civil war in 1967 he fled to Mamfe in Cameroon. There he worked as a band boy for a Congolese group, carried instruments to gigs and got to know Congolese rumba. He taught himself conga, bass guitar and the Congolese finger-picking style on electric guitar. In 1970 he crossed the border, by a bush path, into Nigeria, and ended up in Onitsha.

With his band Rocafil Jazz he recorded Sweet Mother. The song is his best-known and is described as the best-selling song ever by an African artist. It appeared in 1976, on the album Prince Nico Mbarga And Rocafil Jazz. Later came Cool Money (1979) and Let Them Say (1982), among others. Mbarga died in 1997. Sweet Mother is an ode to the mother, a theme that speaks to everyone in West Africa.
artiest/prince-nico-mbarga-en-rocafil-ja.listen: Listen to Sweet Mother. Notice the bright, light-footed guitar lines and the relaxed singing, and how the band lets you sway along without any hurry.

artiest/prince-paul.text:
Prince Paul, real name Paul Edward Huston, is an American producer, DJ and artist from Amityville in New York State. He was born in 1967 and as a teenager began DJing at parties, including with Biz Markie. In 1984 he became the DJ of the hip hop group Stetsasonic. After that he grew into one of the innovative producers of hip hop.

His biggest breakthrough was 3 Feet High and Rising from 1989, the debut album of De La Soul. On it Prince Paul set samples from widely varying sources side by side and added comic sketches, so that the album sounded like a playful collage. He also worked on De La Soul Is Dead and Buhloone Mindstate. He also produced for 3rd Bass, Boogie Down Productions and Big Daddy Kane, among others. With Frukwan, Too Poetic and RZA he formed Gravediggaz, who released an album in 1994. He also made solo work, such as Psychoanalysis: What Is It? and A Prince Among Thieves from 1999.

Prince Paul showed that hip hop could also be humour, narrative and the art of sampling, and not only tough talk. His approach had an effect on many later producers. In the course he is the man behind the funny, layered sound of De La Soul.
artiest/prince-paul.listen: Listen to a track from 3 Feet High and Rising and notice the samples and the short sketches between the songs. Which sounds do you recognise, and where does the record make a joke?

artiest/procol-harum.text:
Procol Harum was an English rock band from Southend-on-Sea in Essex, formed in 1967. The singer and pianist Gary Brooker had earlier been in The Paramounts and wanted to concentrate on writing. Through a friend he met the lyricist Keith Reid. When nobody wanted to record their songs, they started a band themselves, with Matthew Fisher on organ, among others. The name came from a Burmese cat belonging to an acquaintance. Because of a mistake on the telephone, the pedigree name Procul Harun was written down wrongly.

In April 1967 the group recorded its first single in London: A Whiter Shade of Pale. The song is built like baroque music. On the Hammond organ Fisher plays a countermelody loosely based on the third orchestral suite by Johann Sebastian Bach. Underneath runs a slowly descending bass line, and Brooker sings Reid's enigmatic lyrics. Listeners of the pirate station Radio London responded so enthusiastically that the record company rushed the single out. It spent six weeks at number 1 in England and became a worldwide success. More than ten million copies have been sold.

Homburg, among others, followed, but nothing again as big as the debut single. The music of Procol Harum is counted as psychedelic rock and early prog rock, with influences of blues, soul and classical music. With A Whiter Shade of Pale the band showed that the Hammond organ and Bach could have a place in pop music. In 2018 the song was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/procol-harum.listen: Listen to A Whiter Shade of Pale and follow the melody of the Hammond organ, which sounds right at the start and keeps returning. Notice also the bass line, which moves downwards step by step as in baroque music.

artiest/prodromos-tsaousakis.text:
Prodromos Tsaousakis, really Prodromos Moutafoglou, was a popular Greek rebetiko singer, songwriter and composer. He was born in 1919 in Constantinople and at the age of three moved with his family to Thessaloniki. At a young age he became a professional wrestler. In 1940 he volunteered for the Greek army. During the Greco-Italian War he was promoted to sergeant for his courage, and that is how he got the nickname Tsaousakis, derived from the Turkish word for sergeant. During the German occupation he was arrested and tortured.

In 1942 he met Anna Kadoglou, whom he married a year later. He was then singing with various bands in Thessaloniki and got to know Vassilis Tsitsanis. His recording career began in 1946 and he quickly became famous. Until 1951 he worked with Tsitsanis, who wrote several of his best-known songs with his voice in mind. Later he also worked with other composers, such as Giannis Papaioannou, Giorgos Mitsakis and Apostolos Kaldaras.

From 1955 his career went downhill, partly because of the rise of Stelios Kazantzidis. Tsaousakis died in 1979 of a heart attack in Kallithea. His voice belongs to the rebetiko of the 1940s, the Greek urban music that developed from the world of port cities and working-class neighbourhoods. His collaboration with Tsitsanis was the most important of his career.
artiest/prodromos-tsaousakis.listen: Listen to a recording of Tsaousakis with songs by Tsitsanis and notice the bouzouki and the singing voice. Try to hear how the singing follows the melody and improvises around it.

artiest/prodromos-tsaousakis-en-vassilis.text:
Vassilis Tsitsanis was born in 1915 in Trikala, in Greece. He was a songwriter and bouzouki player, and is regarded as one of the founders of modern rebetiko and laiko. His family came from Epirus. As a boy he learned violin, mandola and mandolin, instruments that kept recurring in many of his songs. In 1936 he went to Athens to study law, and a year later he had also learned to play the bouzouki and made his first recording. In 1938 he moved to Thessaloniki, where he stayed for about ten years, including during the German occupation. There he became famous, opened an ouzeri and wrote many of his best songs. When the Germans closed the record companies in 1941, he had already recorded about a hundred songs of his own.

In 1946 he returned to Athens and recorded many of his own compositions. In doing so he made singers famous, among them Sotiria Bellou, Marika Ninou, Ioanna Georgakopoulou and Prodromos Tsaousakis. Tsitsanis made rebetiko more Western and brought it to large parts of the population. In this way he laid the foundation for the later laiko. Synnefiasmeni Kyriaki, which the course mentions, dates from 1948 and belongs to that period, in which Tsaousakis was one of the singers.

Tsitsanis wrote more than five hundred songs. He died in 1984 in London, on his sixty-ninth birthday, after a lung operation. All of Greece mourned, and he is still regarded as a legend of rebetiko. The local source file says nothing further about Tsaousakis himself, so this text follows mainly Tsitsanis.
artiest/prodromos-tsaousakis-en-vassilis.listen: Listen to Synnefiasmeni Kyriaki. Notice the bright, metallic sound of the bouzouki and how the singing voice hovers above it, soft and almost plaintive.

artiest/psy.text:
Psy is the stage name of Park Jae-sang, a South Korean singer, songwriter and producer, born on 31 December 1977 in the Gangnam district of Seoul. He came from a wealthy family and was known at school as the class clown. At fifteen a Korean TV broadcast introduced him to Western pop music, through the concert video Queen Live at Wembley Stadium. In 1996 he began a business studies course in Boston, intended to prepare him to take over his father's company. He preferred to spend his money on a keyboard, a computer and a MIDI interface, and abandoned the course.

His debut album Psy from the Psycho World! appeared in 2001. The worldwide breakthrough came in 2012 with Gangnam Style, a single that reached the top ten of the American Billboard Hot 100 and became a viral sensation. It was the first video on YouTube with a billion views and remained the most-watched video from November 2012 until July 2017. Its successor Gentleman from 2013 also reached the top ten, and the video broke the record for the most viewers in the first twenty-four hours. He founded the talent agency P Nation and received a Korean cultural award.

He turned a song that is largely in Korean into a worldwide hit and showed how quickly a video clip can make a pop star.
artiest/psy.listen: Listen to Gangnam Style and notice how the repeating electronic beat and the short hook together carry the song.

artiest/public-enemy.text:
Public Enemy is an American hip hop group, formed in 1985 in Roosevelt on Long Island, New York. Chuck D and Flavor Flav met at university. Chuck D worked at a student radio station, and his tape Public Enemy Number One caught the attention of the producer Rick Rubin of Def Jam. Around him a group took shape with the production team The Bomb Squad of the brothers Hank and Keith Shocklee and Eric Sadler, DJ Terminator X, Professor Griff and the S1Ws, a uniformed bodyguard on stage.

After the debut Yo! Bum Rush the Show (1987) came It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back (1988), with Bring the Noise, Don't Believe the Hype and Night of the Living Baseheads. It was the first hip hop album to be chosen album of the year in the big critics' poll of The Village Voice. The Bomb Squad's sound was unprecedentedly full: layers of samples, sirens, scratches and noise, with Chuck D's deep, authoritative voice and Flavor Flav's funny exclamations as a counterweight. The lyrics dealt with racism, the media, drugs and the position of Black Americans.

Fear of a Black Planet (1990) became their most successful album. It contains Fight the Power, which became the theme tune of Spike Lee's film Do the Right Thing and is regarded as one of the most influential songs in hip hop history. Public Enemy turned rap into a political voice and has been in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame since 2013.
artiest/public-enemy.listen: Listen to Night of the Living Baseheads and try to pick the layers in the music apart: how many different samples, horns and scratches do you hear at once? Notice how Chuck D's voice cuts straight through them.

artiest/purandara-dasa.text:
Purandara Dasa (about 1470 to about 1564) was a composer, singer and philosopher from what is now Karnataka in India. He was a Haridasa, a servant of Vishnu or Krishna, and followed the Dvaita philosophy of Madhvacharya. He is seen as one of the founders of modern Carnatic music and is called the Pitamaha, the grandfather, of that music. There is debate about his birthplace. In 2018 a committee of the Karnataka government designated Tirthahalli as the most likely place. His year of birth is not certain; the year of death, 1564, comes from his son Madhvapati.

According to tradition he was a rich trader in gold, silver and jewels, who gave away all his possessions to become a devotional singer. He made the difficult Sanskrit teaching of the Bhagavata Purana accessible to everyone in simple, melodic songs. He was one of the most important music scholars of medieval India and devised the basic course for teaching Carnatic music: step-by-step exercises called Svaravalis and Alankaras.

His exercises form the basis of Carnatic music. His influence therefore lies not only in his songs, but also in the way the tradition is handed on.
artiest/purandara-dasa.listen: Listen to a simple Carnatic song by Purandara Dasa and notice the clear, singing melody with a rhythmic pattern that keeps returning. Try to hear how a song consists mainly of repetition and slight variation.

artiest/pussy-riot.text:
Pussy Riot is a Russian feminist protest and performance group, founded in the autumn of 2011 by the then twenty-two-year-old Nadya Tolokonnikova. In all the group had about eleven women. Some of the members came from the art collective Voina. In 2011 Tolokonnikova and Samutsevich gave a lecture on punk feminism, and the group grew out of it. The members played unannounced, provocative guitar shows in public places. These were filmed as video clips and put on the internet. The music began as provocative punk rock and later became more accessible.

The lyrics dealt with feminism, LGBTQ rights and opposition to President Vladimir Putin, his policies and his ties with the Russian Orthodox Church. In February 2012 five members performed in the Cathedral of Christ the Saviour in Moscow. The church condemned it as sacrilege. Three members were arrested, tried and convicted, later receiving an amnesty and being released on conditions. The trial and the sentence attracted a great deal of attention and criticism, especially in the West. Human rights groups such as Amnesty International regarded the women as prisoners of conscience, and many well-known artists spoke up for them. Russian public opinion was on the whole less sympathetic.

In December 2025 the Russian Ministry of Justice put Pussy Riot on the list of extremist organisations. The group shows how punk as a form of protest is still used politically in the twenty-first century, with the public performance as a weapon.
artiest/pussy-riot.listen: Listen to a song by Pussy Riot and notice the raw punk sound and what the lyrics say. Try to hear what role the vocals play.

artiest/pygmalion.text:
Pygmalion is a music ensemble that Raphaël Pichon founded in 2006 while studying at the Conservatoire de Paris. It consists of a choir and an instrumental ensemble and specialises in baroque music, played on authentic instruments of the period. In 2026 it performed at the Adelaide Festival, with three concerts, the group's first performances in Australia.

At first Pygmalion recorded for Alpha, a French label for early music. Since 2014 the recordings have been released on Harmonia Mundi. Besides French repertoire the ensemble has released well-known performances of Johann Sebastian Bach. The series began at Alpha with the missae breves, BWV 233 to 236, the first part of which received a Diapason d'Or in 2008. In 2012 the Mass in B minor, BWV 232, appeared. On Harmonia Mundi there followed in 2014 the Köthener Trauermusik, BWV 244a, a lost cantata by Bach, in 2020 six motets, BWV 225 to 230, which received an Opus Klassik, and in 2022 the Matthäus-Passion.

Pygmalion belongs to the generation of ensembles that perform early music in a historically informed way. Because choir and orchestra belong together, the ensemble can match the sound of voices and instruments to each other.
artiest/pygmalion.listen: Listen to the beginning of Bach's Mass in B minor by Pygmalion and notice how choir and orchestra complement each other. Try to hear how the authentic instruments sound compared with a modern orchestra.
